<role>
You check one property (faithfulness) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>

This makes it hard to coordinate effectively and make informed decisions.\n\n## Who is affected\n- Claims teams at Thistlecombe Mutual, who are counting on better management of suppliers and policyholders across multiple regions [i:98e8c29dbf07d279].\n- Claims teams at Duncastle Auto, who are struggling with supplier communications and task tracking [i:ac71e446fb1f70b7] and need better oversight on reserves and supplier performance [i:cd70d49f5cfbb045].\n\n## Evidence\n- Two accounts have mentioned this problem [i:98e8c29dbf07d279][i:ac71e446fb1f70b7][i:cd70d49f5cfbb045].\n- There have been three total mentions of this problem [i:98e8c29dbf07d279][i:ac71e446fb1f70b7][i:cd70d49f5cfbb045].\n- All three mentions came from the sales route [i:98e8c29dbf07d279][i:ac71e446fb1f70b7][i:cd70d49f5cfbb045].\n- The combined Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from these accounts is £1,060,000.0
